output.title: BLE disconnect step-change isolated to firmware 1.4.2
output.summary: Fleet BLE disconnect rate jumped from a stable ~1.5/device-day baseline (all trains, current and prior windows) to 10.53/device-day on firmware 1.4.2 in the current window. The 1.4.1+app 3.2 resolver cell (devices that share the app 3.2 scheduler rewrite but kept the older firmware supervisor) stayed at 1.5417/device-day, matching historical baseline. This isolates the spike to the 1.4.2 firmware's supervisor-timeout/backoff change rather than to app 3.2's scheduler rewrite or to regional RF environment. Feedback volume (70 connectivity tickets, all firmware 1.4.2/app 3.2) corroborates the magnitude.

leading_hypothesis.statement: The 1.4.2 firmware change (supervision timeout 4s→2s, retry backoff linear→exponential 250ms cap) caused a step-change increase in BLE disconnects, confirmed by the 1.4.1+app3.2 resolver cell remaining at baseline.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: The app 3.2 background scheduler rewrite, not the firmware, is driving the disconnect spike.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Resolver cell 1.4.1+3.2 shows rate 1.5417, indistinguishable from historical baseline, while 1.4.2+3.2 shows 10.53 — app version held constant, firmware varies, effect tracks firmware.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: Dense-office BLE chatter (KI-RF-003) or regional RF environment explains the elevated count.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: KI-RF-003 magnitude is single-digit additions on all trains; observed 1.4.2 rate (10.53) is a 7x jump over baseline across all five regions, exceeding the known office-chatter envelope.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: This mirrors the previously-overturned 1.3.0 disconnect scare (INC-2025-014), where firmware was wrongly blamed.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: INC-2025-014 was falsified using a same-phone hold-out on 1.2.0 showing the same burst; here the 1.4.1+3.2 resolver cell (same app, different firmware) does NOT show the burst, which is the opposite signature.

recommended_actions.description: Escalate to firmware engineering to re-characterize 1.4.2 supervisor timeout/backoff change against outdoor, body-block, and commuting RF conditions (not just indoor soak lab).
Prepare staged rollback path from 1.4.2 to 1.4.1 via factory tool for the affected cohort pending root-cause confirmation.
Continue collecting 1.4.1-control same-household splits per support playbook to further corroborate the firmware-specific signature before any customer communication.

uncertainty: 1.4.2 has no prior-window baseline (it shipped inside the current window), so the comparison relies on cross-sectional resolver cells rather than a true before/after on the same train.

Soak lab data for 1.4.2 only covered indoor office RF; outdoor/body-block field conditions were not re-characterized at ship, so the mechanism (vs. just the correlation) is not yet fully confirmed at the component level.

output.title: Skin-irritation and adhesion feedback consistent with existing open characterization
output.summary: Adhesion-flag telemetry shows only a modest fleet-wide increase (0.1358 current vs 0.1250 prior) with no firmware or region standing out sharply; 1.4.2's current rate (0.1367) is close to 1.4.1's prior rate (0.1364). Feedback volume spans nearly every firmware and region with recurring themes of high-motion lift, sweat, and heat — matching the already-open KI-AD-007 mechanism (high motion_intensity + elevated skin_temp_delta_c) rather than pointing to a single new defect or lot.

leading_hypothesis.statement: Reported adhesion/skin-irritation feedback reflects the pre-existing, open high-motion adhesive lift characterization (KI-AD-007), not a new firmware- or lot-specific defect.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A new adhesive lot defect is driving the cluster, similar to the confirmed INC-2025-031 lot incident.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Pull lot codes from affected devices' pouches and check retained-sample peel strength against unaffected lots in the same firmware window; INC-2025-031 was only closed once a specific lot failed retained testing.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: Firmware 1.4.2 specifically elevates adhesion flags via some sensor/heuristic change.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: 1.4.2's current adhesion rate (0.1367) is in the same band as other firmware trains current and prior; KD-02 states the adhesion-flag heuristic was unchanged in 1.4.2.

recommended_actions.description: Escalate the feedback cluster to Quality for a lot-code split to rule in/out a repeat of the INC-2025-031 pattern before treating this as characteristic-only.
Continue routing tickets through the adhesion queue with replacement rings offered; do not close tickets as expected behavior per playbook guidance.

uncertainty: No lot-code field is present in the telemetry export provided, so a lot-specific defect (as in INC-2025-031) cannot be ruled in or out from this data alone.

The modest fleet-wide increase (0.1250→0.1358) could reflect seasonal activity increase rather than any device-side change; no motion_intensity or skin_temp_delta_c cross-tab was available to test the KI-AD-007 mechanism directly against this feedback set.

output.title: Wellness-score misread as clinical result — recurring claims-interpretation pattern
output.summary: Eighteen feedback tickets across firmware 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.4.0, 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 and across all five regions describe the readiness score being treated as a clinical/medical result (e.g., 'medical result', 'health verdict', 'lab result'). This matches the documented, previously-confirmed communications-risk pattern (KD-06 INC-2025-002) rather than a hardware or scoring defect. Five other tickets in the same window explicitly confirm wearers correctly understood the score as wellness-only after clarification, indicating the confusion is copy/perception-driven and not universal.

leading_hypothesis.statement: A recurring subset of wearers interpret the readiness score/tile as a clinical finding, consistent with the documented claims-misread pattern rather than any scoring or hardware defect.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A specific app or firmware release introduced new clinical-sounding copy that caused the misread.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: KD-05 records that app 3.2's copy review (2026-05-02) added no new clinical vocabulary, and misread tickets appear across firmware/app combinations spanning multiple release trains, not concentrated on one.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: The scoring algorithm itself is producing anomalous or out-of-family values that resemble clinical flags.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: KD-06 INC-2025-002 closure established the integer score was in-family and no scoring rollback was needed; nothing in this feedback set describes an out-of-range score value.

recommended_actions.description: Reinforce the claims-misread support script (KD-03) with staff and confirm no medical-advice language is used on threads.
Flag on-screen readiness copy for another Communications/Legal review to see if additional wellness-only framing could reduce misread rate, per KD-05 section 7.1.

uncertainty: This is a communications-risk finding, not a clinical or hardware determination; this record does not assess or comment on any wearer's health status.
The dataset does not indicate whether misread volume is rising or falling over time since only a single current window is available with no comparable prior-window claims tag breakdown.

output.title: Overheating-tagged feedback traced to Nordics regional battery drain and red battery UI chrome
output.summary: All 50 overheating-tagged feedback records originate from the Nordics region and describe cold-weather battery drain alongside warmth/heat language and an alarming red battery/sync screen. Telemetry confirms Nordics battery_drain_pct (17.28% current) is elevated versus other regions (~12.9%) but this is a long-standing, stable regional characteristic (KI-NW-014), present in both current and prior windows and not a new step. skin_temp_delta_c in Nordics (1.35°C) is not elevated versus other regions and does not correlate with drain, ruling out a thermal/patch-temperature explanation. The 'overheating' language is best explained by the documented cosmetic UI chrome issue (KI-UI-011: harsh red battery fill below 40%).

leading_hypothesis.statement: Overheating-tagged tickets reflect the known Nordics battery-drain regional characteristic (KI-NW-014) combined with the cosmetic red-battery UI chrome (KI-UI-011), not an actual thermal or hardware defect.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: There is a genuine thermal/hardware defect causing devices or phones to run hot.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: skin_temp_delta_c shows no elevation in Nordics (1.35°C vs UK 1.31°C) and near-zero correlation with battery drain (-0.04); the operations export has no ambient/thermal channel to support a thermal-rail claim, and all values are within typical field range.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: This is a new, firmware-driven battery/thermal regression coinciding with 1.4.2.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: 1.4.2's own mean drain across all regions (~14.1%) is in line with 1.4.1 (~13.9%); the Nordics elevation is present across firmware 1.2.0 through 1.4.2 and in both current and prior windows, indicating a regional, not firmware, effect.
